title: Heavy Metal Pt II
summary: Part two of the heavy metal episodes. The hosts cover Ozzy Osbourne's notorious stunts and his firing from Black Sabbath, the PMRC and its Filthy Fifteen list, MTV and Headbanger's Ball, the diversity of metal bands, metal guitar culture and the BC Rich guitar, Lord of the Rings references, and metal's social and political messages. They discuss studies on metal listeners' brains and personality, the metal subgenres (mathcore, mathrock, metalcore, extreme metal), and album cover art. The episode closes with the 1982 death of Randy Rhoads in a plane crash, kawaii metal, Rolling Stone's top ten metal albums list, and recommendations of books and horror films.
topics: Lord of the Rings in metal
Stuff You Should Know heavy metal part two

segments.title: Opening banter and part two kickoff
segments.summary: Hosts introduce part two of the heavy metal episodes and make jokes about a Black Sabbath lyric.

segments.title: Ozzy Osbourne stunts and firing from Sabbath
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Ozzy Osbourne's bat and dove biting incidents, the reported story of a dead bat thrown on stage in Des Moines, and why he was pushed out of Black Sabbath for being hard to work with.

segments.title: PMRC, Filthy Fifteen and the sticker
segments.summary: The hosts describe the PMRC led by Tipper Gore and its Filthy Fifteen list, where most entries were metal or hard rock. They argue the targets were unjustified and note the resulting explicit lyrics warning sticker.

segments.title: MTV, Headbanger's Ball and metal on television
segments.summary: The hosts discuss MTV's eclectic rotation, the early Iron Maiden videos, the move of metal to Headbanger's Ball hosted by Ricky Rockman, and its concert tours.

segments.title: Diversity in metal and hair metal bands
segments.summary: The hosts talk about metal's demographics and bands such as Bad Brains, Body Count, Living Colour, The Darkness, and Fishbone, plus hair metal.

segments.title: Women in metal and leather style
segments.summary: The hosts mention women in metal such as Angela Gossow, Alissa White-Gluz, and Nita Strauss, then discuss the leather and studs look and its origin in gay BDSM clubs linked to Rob Halford.

segments.title: Metal tropes: umlauts, classical influence, and musicianship
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the decorative umlaut, Richard Meltzer's claimed role in it, classical music influence on metal guitarists, and the technical skill needed to play metal.

segments.title: Guitars and gear: BC Rich
segments.summary: The hosts discuss guitar magazines, teachers, and the BC Rich guitar models including the flying bee.

segments.title: Lord of the Rings, Burzum and black metal fonts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Lord of the Rings references in metal, the Burzum project and its name, and the gothic black letter typeface used on metal album logos.
topics: Lord of the Rings in metal

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Break before the next section on metal's social views and brain studies.

segments.title: Metal's social and political messages
segments.summary: The hosts argue metal lyrics are often populist, anti-authoritarian, and anti-war, citing Metallica songs, Megadeth's Peace Sells, the Pantera Nazi salute incident, and left-leaning grindcore bands.

segments.title: Metal and the brain: studies on listeners
segments.summary: The hosts discuss research on how metal engages the brain, helps focus for some people with ADHD or autism, and studies of metalheads' personality traits and reactions to violent imagery.

segments.title: Metal subgenres: mathcore, mathrock, metalcore
segments.summary: The hosts break down mathcore as a combination of mathrock and metalcore, explain extreme metal's subgenres, and note how finely divided metal is.

segments.title: Album cover art
segments.summary: The hosts discuss metal album art, citing Black Sabbath's debut cover, Iron Maiden and Derek Riggs, Metallica's Master of Puppets, Slayer's Reign in Blood, Dio's Holy Diver with mascot Murray, and Rainbow's Rising.

segments.title: Guns N' Roses cover, Quiet Riot and Metal Health
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the controversial Appetite for Destruction cover and its inner sleeve, and Quiet Riot's Metal Health reaching number one as the first metal band to top the charts.

segments.title: Death of Randy Rhoads
segments.summary: The hosts recount Randy Rhoads' career from Quiet Riot to Ozzy Osbourne's band, the Leesburg, Florida plane crash in March 1982 in which Andrew Aycock flew a Beechcraft Bonanza that clipped the tour bus, killing Rhoads and Rachel Youngblood, and the effect on Ozzy.

segments.title: Kawaii metal and Rolling Stone's top metal albums
segments.summary: The hosts introduce kawaii metal with Babymetal and Lady Baby, then read Rolling Stone's top ten metal albums list, with Black Sabbath's Paranoid at number one.

segments.title: Book and horror movie recommendations
segments.summary: Instead of listener mail, the hosts recommend Keith Rosson's books Fever House, The Devil by Name, and Coffin Moon, plus horror films Best Wishes to All and Red Rooms.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite email feedback about heavy metal and close the episode.
